assertion.statement: For every real x>=1 there is a prime p with x<p<=2x.
assertion.objects: Real x and an ordinary positive rational prime p.
assertion.hypotheses: x>=1; at the consumer x=CN with fixed integer C>16 and positive integer N.
assertion.quantifiers: Every positive N uses the same fixed C; a prime P may depend on N.
assertion.parameter_range: All positive N, including bounded N; no asymptotic threshold.
assertion.uniformity: The interval ratio is uniformly between C and2C, independent of N.
assertion.constants: No new constants: the fixed C already in the base proof is used unchanged.
assertion.normalizations: For integral CN>1, 2CN is composite, changing the supplied upper weak inequality into the consumer strict one.
assertion.exceptional_cases: N=1 is included because C>16; no residue-class constraint is asserted.
assertion.limit_order: Fix C first, then for each N select P. No new cutoff or limiting order.
